metadata.title: What Could Really Power Microsoft Stock Higher From Here?

content.text:
What looks like another AI product is actually a fundamental and potentially lucrative shift in how the company makes its money.
For a company at the center of the AI universe, Microsoft (MSFT) stock has been surprisingly earthbound lately. It's down about 20% over the past year and trades 28% below its 52-week high. With so much attention on new features, you might be wondering what could actually provide the fuel for a sustained climb from here.
The answer lies in a quiet but profound shift in the company's entire business model, one that could unlock a new layer of growth on top of its substantial existing customer base.
The New Engine: A "Per User and Usage" Business
For decades, Microsoft sold you software. Now, it's moving to a model where it sells you outcomes. The company's own management describes the transformation as moving to a "per user and usage business." Think about that. It's one thing to sell a subscription for access to a tool; it's another thing entirely to get paid for every single task that tool performs. The goal extends beyond simply adding more seats to capturing a fraction of the value from the billions of queries, reports, and summaries its AI agents will run. This model, if successful, could fundamentally re-rate what each of Microsoft's hundreds of millions of users is worth.
Is anyone actually paying for this?
A great strategy is one thing, but execution is another. The early evidence for this new model comes from the front lines of its AI push: Microsoft 365 Copilot. The company now has "over 20 million Microsoft 365 Copilot paid seats," a number that's accelerating. In the most recent quarter, seat additions increased 250% year-over-year, representing the fastest growth since the product's launch. This isn't a hypothetical; it's a real, paying customer base that is rapidly adopting the very consumption-based products that represent the company's future. We have also explored how this could impact the stock's valuation. If you'd rather own the whole technology space than bet on a single giant, a technology ETF like VGT holds Microsoft among its largest positions.
The Price Tag Is $190 Billion
Microsoft is backing this strategic shift with an immense amount of capital. The company expects to invest roughly $190 billion in capital expenditures in calendar year 2026 alone. That significant figure is allocated for building the global engine required to power all that new, paid usage, a task that goes far beyond constructing more data centers. The company has been clear that even with this spending, strong customer demand continues to exceed available capacity. It's a classic growth story: invest heavily to meet overwhelming demand that you can directly monetize. This spending is the clearest signal of management's conviction in the per-user, per-usage future.
